findings.title: Client mutation calls `.json()` on a 204 No Content response
findings.rationale: The server route `POST /pulls/:id/findings/dismiss-suggestions` returns HTTP 204 with no body. The client mutation function calls `res.json()` on the fetch response, which will reject because there is no content to parse. This causes the mutation to always fail, the `onSuccess` callback never runs, and the query invalidation never happens. The button appears to do nothing and the user may see an unhandled error.

findings.title: Query invalidation key may not match findings query
findings.rationale: The `onSuccess` handler invalidates queries with key `['reviews', prId]`. If the findings panel uses a different query key (e.g. `['findings', prId]`), the panel will not refresh after dismissal. This is a silent data staleness bug.

findings.title: Mutation lacks error handling and user feedback
findings.rationale: The `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation does not handle errors. If the request fails (network error, server error), the user receives no feedback. The button is disabled while pending but remains disabled on error unless reset.

findings.title: Button lacks styling and accessibility attributes
findings.rationale: The new dismiss-all button has no CSS classes, no `aria-label`, and no keyboard handling beyond native button behavior. It may not match the existing toolbar styling and is not accessible to screen readers.

matched_title: Client calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response

findings.title: Client calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response
findings.rationale: The server route returns HTTP 204 with no body. The client mutation calls `return res.json();` which attempts to parse the empty response body as JSON, throwing a `SyntaxError`. This prevents the mutation from ever succeeding, so the bulk-dismiss feature is broken for all users. The caller is the `FindingsPanel` component that invokes `dismissSuggestions.mutate(prId)`.

findings.title: Client mutation does not check `res.ok` before parsing JSON
findings.rationale: The mutation calls `res.json()` unconditionally. If the server returns an error status (e.g., 400, 401, 500) with a JSON error body, `fetch` does not reject, so `res.json()` will succeed and the mutation will resolve with the error payload. The `onSuccess` callback will then run, invalidating the queries as if the operation succeeded, leading to stale data and no user-visible error. The caller relies on the mutation's success/failure to update UI state.

findings.title: No error feedback in the UI for the bulk-dismiss action
findings.rationale: The button disables while the mutation is pending, but there is no visual feedback if the mutation fails (e.g., network error or server error). Users may click the button, see it briefly disable, and then re-enable with no indication of success or failure. Consider showing a toast or inline error message.

findings.title: Missing database migration for new `tags` column
findings.rationale: The contract adds a `tags` field that will be persisted in the database, but no Drizzle migration is included in this PR. Without a corresponding column (with a default of `NULL`), the server will fail to insert or update findings that include tags. The PR description claims existing findings keep working, which is true only if the column already exists or is added separately. This is a WARNING because the contract change is incomplete without the schema migration.

findings.title: Use stable key for tag rendering to avoid React key conflicts
findings.rationale: The tag spans use `key={tag}`, which will cause duplicate-key warnings if two tags have the same string value. While unlikely in practice, using the array index or a combination of tag and index would be more robust.

findings.title: Add per-tag length constraint to prevent abuse
findings.rationale: The schema enforces a maximum of 5 tags but does not limit the length of each individual tag string. A malicious or careless client could send very long strings (e.g., 10k characters) that might cause storage or rendering issues. The PR description mentions 'short strings' but does not enforce it.

matched_title: New response field may break strict parsers

findings.title: New response field may break strict parsers
findings.rationale: Adding `tags` to the `Finding` object changes the shape of every response that includes a finding. While the shared contract uses `z.object` (which ignores unknown keys), any consumer that uses strict parsing (e.g., `z.strictObject`, `zod-to-json-schema` with `additionalProperties: false`, or a hand-written parser that rejects unknown fields) will now fail on responses containing a finding. This is a contract addition that narrows what consumers can rely on. Although the field is optional and nullish, the change is not backwards-compatible for strict parsers.

findings.title: Individual tag string length not constrained
findings.rationale: The PR description mentions 'short strings' but the schema only limits the array length to 5, not the length of each string. Without a `.max()` on the string itself, a client could send tags that are arbitrarily long (e.g., 10KB each), which could bloat responses and cause rendering issues in the UI chips.

matched_title: Duplicate tag values cause React key collision

findings.title: Duplicate tag values cause React key collision
findings.rationale: The rendering uses `key={tag}` on each tag chip. If a finding contains duplicate tag strings (e.g. `["flaky", "flaky"]`), React will emit a duplicate key warning and may render incorrectly. The schema allows duplicate strings, so the client must handle them. Use `key={index}` or a combination of tag and index.

findings.title: Tags array items lack length validation
findings.rationale: The PR description mentions 'short strings', but the schema only limits the array to 5 items, not the length of each string. Very long strings could break UI layout or storage. Consider adding `.max(20)` or similar to each string element.
